episode_title: Stock Market Suffers Historic $2.5T Loss & How Steve Kornacki Won the Midterms
question: Why did the Nasdaq fall 5.5% on the day the stock market lost $2 trillion, and what stocks drove the decline?
transcript_excerpt: The Nasdaq fell 5.5% driven by a massive unwinding of the AI trade. Chipmaker and AI-related stocks that had been propelling the market higher suddenly dragged it down: NVIDIA fell 9%, Broadcom fell 10%, Qualcomm dropped 13%, Tesla and SpaceX both had nearly 10% wipeouts, and companies like CoreWeave, Nebius, and IRON fell more than 15% each.

question: How many data center proposals passed in Tuesday's elections, and what does that signal about AI infrastructure expansion?
transcript_excerpt: Of the 45 data center related proposals on ballots across the country on Tuesday, 44 landed on the anti-data center side, with only one passing in Harwood, North Dakota with just 800 people. This represents a major setback because more than 40 percent of all planned data center capacity is slated to come online in Texas, Georgia, and Ohio—all states where newly elected governors are antagonistic to data centers.

question: How many views did Steve Kornacki's dedicated election night stream achieve across platforms?
transcript_excerpt: Kornacki Cam, a dedicated stream focused solely on Kornacki and his analysis that ran nearly 11 hours, earned a record 29 million views across all platforms Tuesday evening and 6.1 million views on YouTube, topping all streams.

question: How many AI agent rides were booked on Uber during Halloween week, one of the busiest weeks of the year?
transcript_excerpt: During Uber's third quarter earnings call, their CFO revealed that during Halloween week, one of Uber's busiest weeks of the year, the total number of Uber rides booked by AI agents was four. While 50 people did order Uber Eats using an agent, considering Uber processed 320 million rides and eats orders that weekend, this is negligible.

question: What percentage of US gamers intend to buy Grand Theft Auto 6, and how does this compare to the Zelda Ocarina of Time release?
transcript_excerpt: Nearly 30% of US gamers said they intend to buy Grand Theft Auto 6, making it the biggest game the industry has ever seen. However, Nintendo released The Legend of Zelda Ocarina of Time on the same day—expected to be the second biggest video game launch this year—potentially creating a Barbenheimer effect where two huge simultaneous entertainment releases lift demand for both rather than cannibalize each other.
